definition: A model that fits its training data extremely well but generalizes poorly to new data.
details: Overfitting occurs when a model is powerful enough to memorize noise and idiosyncrasies in the training set instead of learning underlying structure. It is guarded against with regularization, data augmentation, early stopping, dropout and evaluation on held-out validation and test sets.

explainer.lead: Overfitting is when a model fits its training data extremely well but generalizes poorly to new data. It is the central risk whenever model capacity outpaces the information in the data.

tiers.eli5: It is like a student who memorizes the exact wording of practice problems but freezes when the exam uses different numbers.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers guard against it with regularization, data augmentation, early stopping, dropout, and evaluation on held-out validation and test sets. A pitfall is tuning repeatedly on the validation set until it, too, becomes a training signal.
tiers.paperLevel: Overfitting occurs when a model is powerful enough to memorize noise and idiosyncrasies in the training set instead of learning underlying structure; it is countered by the listed techniques and held-out evaluation.

explainer.example: A deep network reaches near-zero training loss yet scores far worse on the test set, showing it learned noise rather than structure.
